title: Knowing the User Is Not Knowing What We Established: Grounding Awareness in Personal Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.18684v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Personal-agent memory has largely focused on learning what users know, prefer, and want. However, knowing the user does not necessarily mean knowing what the user and the agent have established together. An assistant's proposal should not become an authorized instruction merely because it is remembered. We introduce Grounding Awareness, the ability to distinguish accepted, unacknowledged, revised, and scoped arrangements when selecting actions. We develop a controlled benchmark to test whether agents can tell the difference between proposals users have accepted and those they have not, and whether they apply accepted arrangements only where appropriate. Across multiple agents and memory systems, we find that strong memory performance does not ensure Grounding Awareness. translated_title: 了解用户并不等于了解我们共同确立的内容：个人智能体中的共识感知
translated_abstract: 个人智能体的记忆研究大多聚焦于学习用户知道什么、偏好什么、想要什么。然而，了解用户并不一定意味着了解用户与智能体共同确立的内容。助手的提议不应仅仅因为被记住就自动成为已授权的指令。我们提出了“共识感知”（Grounding Awareness），即在选择行动时能够区分“已接受”“未被确认”“已修订”和“限定范围”等不同约定状态的能力。我们构建了一个受控基准，用于测试智能体能否区分用户已接受与未接受的提议，以及是否只在适当的范围内应用已接受的约定。在多个智能体和记忆系统上的实验表明，强大的记忆性能并不能保证共识感知。更令人惊讶的是，提供更完整的用户信息反而会增加对未确认提议的执行，而持久记忆可能导致智能体将这些提议视为……
tldr: 本文提出个人智能体应具备“共识感知”能力并构建基准进行评测，发现记忆性能强并不代表智能体能区分用户已接受与未确认的约定，而更完整的用户信息和持久记忆甚至会促使智能体错误执行未被用户认可的提议。
en_tdlr: Introducing "Grounding Awareness" and a controlled benchmark, this paper shows that strong memory does not ensure personal agents distinguish accepted from unacknowledged arrangements, and richer user information or persistent memory can even cause agents to execute unconfirmed proposals.
